response.sql: SELECT o.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, COUNT(*) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.bandusagepct > 47.6 GROUP BY o.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The inner JOIN on observstation drops telescopes with no matching observatory. Each telescope maps to at most one observatory because telescregistry is the primary key, so COUNT(*) counts telescopes.
'High side of a 47.6 cutoff' means strictly greater than 47.6, so a telescope with bandusagepct exactly 47.6 is excluded. The request does not settle the boundary.
Telescopes whose observatory has a NULL lunarstage form their own group with a NULL moon phase, rather than being dropped. Telescopes with a NULL bandusagepct are excluded by the comparison.
Ties in telescope_count at the 10th position are broken arbitrarily, since the request does not specify a secondary sort.

alternatives.interpretation: 'High side' includes the cutoff itself, so telescopes with bandusagepct equal to 47.6 are kept (greater than or equal to).
alternatives.sql: SELECT o.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, COUNT(*) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.bandusagepct >= 47.6 GROUP BY o.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC LIMIT 10;

alternatives.interpretation: Groups with no recorded moon phase (NULL lunarstage) are not moon phases, so they are excluded from the grouping.
